title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Integration, Escalation, Health Checks, and QBR
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the standardized process Redwood Customer Success (CS) and Support teams use to onboard enterprise customers, integrate Redwood products, operate support and escalation, maintain health checks, and run Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for CS managers, solutions engineers, support engineers, and on-call SRE/engineering partners.

Goals

- Deliver predictable, secure, and low-friction onboarding for enterprise customers.
- Ensure rapid incident triage and clear escalation paths for customer-impacting issues.
- Provide repeatable integration checklists and known-issue workarounds to reduce time-to-value.
- Produce consistent health checks and QBR artifacts that demonstrate value and identify risk.

Audience and scope

- Audience: Customer Success, Support, Solutions Engineering, Product, SRE, and Account Executives.
- Scope: Hosted API (redwood-api), Redwood Console, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Redwood Private (VPC/private-control-plane). Excludes internal developer onboarding.

Key SLAs and Support targets

- Response targets (initial acknowledgment):
  1. P0 (Severity: service down for customer production): 15 minutes
  2. P1 (major degradation impacting key features): 1 hour
  3. P2 (partial degradation, non-critical): 4 business hours
  4. P3 (general question/feature request): 1 business day
- Resolution SLOs (target):
  - P0: 4 hours or continuous mitigation until resolved (workaround + cross-team incident).
  - P1: 24 hours (may include temporary workaround).
  - P2: 7 business days.
  - P3: handled in normal product cycle / backlog.
- Uptime SLO for production endpoints (hosted API / console): 99.95% monthly.

Roles and ownership

- Customer Success Manager (CSM): primary customer contact for onboarding milestones, QBRs, and commercial escalations.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical lead for integration, initial architecture, and validation.
- Support Engineer (Tier 1/2): first responders for support tickets; owns triage and initial remediation.
- SRE/Infra On-call: handles platform incidents (redwood-api, dedicated-gateway, private-control-plane) and escalates to engineering if needed.
- Product/Engineering: bug fixes, root cause analysis (RCA), and model-serving regressions.

Onboarding milestones (standard 8-week program)

1. Discovery & Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Kickoff meeting agenda: goals, success metrics, data residency/security requirements, integration owners, and timeline.
   - Deliverables: Onboarding runbook, contact matrix, and access checklist.
2. Architecture & Integration Planning (Week 1-2)
   - SE to produce integration diagram (recommended: redwood-api -> customer-backend; dedicated-gateway for reserved capacity; VPC peering for Private).
   - Validate model selection, throughput targets, and latency SLOs.
3. Implementation & Test (Week 3-5)
   - Provide example code snippets and SDK quickstart.
   - Integration checklist validation (see checklist table).
4. Hardening & Go-live Prep (Week 6-7)
   - Load testing (throughput and spike tests), failure injection, and DR runbook review.
5. Production Cutover & QBR Setup (Week 8)
   - Formal cutover checklist and 30/60/90 day QBR cadence scheduled.

Integration checklist (use this as gate criteria)

| Item | Owner | Success criteria | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| API Key provisioning and RBAC | SE / CSM | Customer can call redwood-api with scoped key | Use least-privilege keys for staging/production |
| Network connectivity & routing | Customer infra / SE | Dedicated: VPC peering successful; Hosted: firewall allowlist in place | Validate egress IPs and region endpoints |
| Data flow & retention policy | CSM / Security | Customer signs data residency and retention plan | Map sensitive fields and masking requirements |
| Rate limits & quota configuration | SE / Support | Quotas applied per contract; burst policies validated | Document throttling behavior |
| Observability & tracing | SE / SRE | App traces show token-level latency and errors | Integrate with customer APM when requested |
| Failover & fallback testing | SE / SRE | Fallback to compatible model or region tested | Confirm acceptable degradation mode |

Escalation playbook (step-by-step)

1. Triage (Support Tier 1)
   - Record customer impact, collect logs, request reproducible example and request-id(s).
   - Attempt standard remediation steps: restart client, validate API key, check quota usage.
2. Escalate to Tier 2 (Support/Solutions Engineering) if unresolved after 30 minutes for P0/P1 or 2 hours for P2
   - Attach full request traces, metrics, and timeline.
   - Open an internal slack channel: #incident-<customer-shortname> and notify on-call SRE.
3. SRE / Infra engagement
   - Run platform diagnostics: node health, GPU utilization, queue depth, KV cache hit rate.
   - If platform issue: create an Incident in the incident tracker and notify stakeholders (CSM, SE, Product).
4. Engineering bug/RCA
   - If code or model regression suspected, escalate to the owning engineering team with priority label and provide clear replication steps and dataset (if allowed).
5. Customer communication cadence
   - P0: Status update every 30 minutes until mitigated.
   - P1: Status update every 2 hours until resolved.
   - P2/P3: Daily updates or as agreed.

Escalation contact matrix (examples)

- Support Slack: #support (triage)
- Incident Slack: #incident-ops and #incident-<customer_shortname>
- Pager (SRE on-call): via PagerDuty (policy: SRE-Platform-Pager)
- Engineering leads: eng-runtime@redwood.com, eng-infra@redwood.com

Known issues and workarounds (common patterns)

- High token-latency on long sequences
  - Symptom: tail latency spikes when sequence length > 2048.
  - Workaround: enable chunked prompting and KV cache pinning; recommend model-variant with optimized long-context kernels (see kernel-and-scheduling docs).
- Intermittent 429 (rate-limited) during bursts
  - Symptom: client receives 429 despite contract burst allowance.
  - Workaround: confirm quota configuration, increase burst window on dedicated pools, or implement exponential backoff client-side.
- Model regression after rollout
  - Symptom: sudden drop in quality or increased hallucination rates after model switch.
  - Workaround: rollback to previous model-version, create evals against canonical prompt-set, and open regression triage (see regression-triage).
- Private deployment connectivity issues
  - Symptom: control-plane cannot reach customer-hosted agents after upgrade.
  - Workaround: validate egress rules, check certificate rotation, and follow onprem-packaging upgrade/rollback runbook.

Support process and ticket lifecycle

- Channels: support portal, support@redwood.com, account CSM, phone for enterprise SLAs.
- Ticket triage steps:
  1. Intake: capture impact, environment, request-id, and attachments.
  2. Categorize: product bug, platform incident, configuration, integration, or request.
  3. Assign: Tier1 or SE + set severity.
  4. Remediate/Escalate: follow escalation playbook.
  5. Close: document resolution and next steps; CSM follows up with QBR items if long-term.

Health checks and QBR materials

- Recommended health check cadence: weekly automated, monthly review with SE, and quarterly with customer (QBR).
- Health check components (weekly):
  - API error rate (5xx) and client-side error rates.
  - Token-level latency P50/P95/P99 by route and model.
  - Throughput and request volume trends.
  - Cost per 1k tokens by model and route.
  - Cache hit rate and effectiveness of batching.
  - Security events: failed auth, suspicious usage patterns.
- QBR template (deliverables):
  1. Executive summary: adoption, value delivered, and top outcomes.
  2. Reliability & performance: uptime, incidents since last QBR, remediation status.
  3. Utilization & economics: cost trends, inefficient routes, recommendations.
  4. Product & roadmap asks: model upgrades, feature requests.
  5. Action items & owners (30/60/90 day plan).

Example QBR checklist (what CS presents)

- Usage highlights (top features and routes)
- SLA performance and recent incidents
- Cost optimization recommendations (batching, quantization, routing rules)
- Next technical milestones and dates
- Agreed success metrics for next quarter

Operational telemetry and dashboards

- Default dashboards teams should configure for each enterprise customer:
  - Per-route latency (P50/P95/P99), token spend, and error rate
  - Model variant performance comparison by workload
  - Quota consumption and upcoming quota exhaustion alerts
  - Cost per 1k tokens and forecast for next 30 days
- Integrations: forward logs/traces to customer S3/Datadog/Databricks as agreed in contract.

Templates and example artifacts

- Kickoff agenda (bulleted)
- Integration runbook checklist (table above)
- Customer cutover checklist (pre-cutover smoke tests, rollback plan, monitoring alerts)
- Incident update email template:

  Subject: [Customer X] Incident update — <short description> (P0/P1)

  Hi <Customer Owner>,

  We wanted to provide a status update on the incident impacting <feature>. Current status: <mitigations in place>. Next update in 30 minutes. Key actions taken: <list>. Owner: <SRE/Support engineer>.

  Regards,
  <CSM name> on behalf of Redwood Support

Where to find linked runbooks and docs

- Integration guides: confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- Onprem packaging and upgrade: confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging
- Regression triage: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage
- Runtime and kernel notes: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling

Change control and major upgrades

- Major behavior changes (e.g., model variant upgrades, quantization format changes) must be communicated 30 days prior to scheduled rollout.
- For private deployments, coordinate control-plane updates with customer windows and require a signed change ticket.

FAQ and troubleshooting quick wins

- "Why am I seeing higher costs after enabling batching?" — Answer: batching can increase short-term token usage for prompt padding; validate batch window size and model selection.
- "Latency spikes on warm caches" — Answer: verify GPU contention, pre-warm KV cache, and validate continuous batching config.

Appendix: example CLI and JSON snippets

- API call example (curl)

  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-large-1","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

- Example quota config (JSON)

  {
    "quota_name": "enterprise-customer-1-prod",
    "rate_limit": "1000/min",
    "burst": "2000",
    "models_allowed": ["redwood-large-1","redwood-medium-2"]
  }

Revision history

If you have questions or require a custom onboarding cadence for a large customer (> $X committed ARR), contact enterprise-ops@redwood.com or your assigned CSM.
